citations.claim: energy trending upward before violation, still below limit
first violating step: energy exceeds allowed 7551.869 (E0*1.1+5)

counterfactual.change: halved dt from 0.0311943 to 0.015 (single field change) - reduces per-step integration error so energy stays within bound; same 4 steps, otherwise identical

explanation: Shrunk case is single high-speed body (vx~37, speed~38-41) with large dt~0.0312 near the 1/30 limit, gravity 9.81, no walls/controller. Semi-implicit Euler with substeps (~41-43/substep) still accumulates positive energy drift each step: E rises from E0 6860.79 to 6998, 7159, 7344, and 7551.94 at step 4, exceeding allowed 1.1*E0+5=7551.87 by ~0.07J. Halving dt removes the drift, showing the violation is numerical energy gain due to coarse integration, not physical work.
vision_note: A single blue body moves steadily rightward across an otherwise empty arena from steps 1 to 4 with no wall collisions, controller, or waypoints visible. At step 4 it is near the right boundary but shows no penetration, tunneling, or sudden jump; the motion looks smooth with no visible source of energy gain.
